We need to find a one-step retrosynthesis route to target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. This appears to be a methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe a methyl ester of a bicyclo[2.2.1]?? Actually structure: COC(=O) attached to a chiral carbon that is part of a bicyclic system with a ketone. So target is methyl ester of a bicyclic ketone (maybe methyl 2-oxabicyclo?). Anyway we need a retrosynthesis with one step, leaves must be commercially available chemicals, total price <= $405. We need to propose a reaction template ID and children (precursor SMILES). We need to ensure they are buyable. We need to find a template that disconnections the ester to methanol + acid (or acid chloride). So precursors: methanol (CO) and the corresponding carboxylic acid: the same skeleton but with COOH instead of COOMe. That acid SMILES: O=C(O)C([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)?? Actually the target is methyl ester of a carboxylic acid attached to the bicyclic ketone. So acid SMILES: O=C(O)C1... Let's generate: Replace "COC(...)=O" with "OC(...)=O". The target SMILES: COC([C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O)=O. The carbonyl carbon is attached to OCH3 and to the chiral carbon. So acid would be O=C(O)[C@]12... So acid SMILES: O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O. Let's test: "O=C(O)[C@]12CC=CC[C@H]1C(C2)=O". That seems plausible.

Now check if acid is commercially available. Use is_buyable.
